answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity has a price. Each agent posts a refundable bond before earning nectar, the network's reward for verified work, so spawning fake peers stops being free. Every bond emits a signed pulse each epoch, a heartbeat referencing the previous one, chaining identity to history fresh keys cannot forge retroactively. Watchers, spread like yarrow through the mesh, sample these pulses and flag duplicates; a confirmed clone burns its bond, paying the reporter a bounty. Cost up front, chained pulses over time, slashing on proof: a million sybils cost a million stakes.
